# BigQuery views

One file per view. Read the file for the view a question is about; the columns, the value
conventions and worked example SQL are all there. Query them with genetics.sql(...) — see
the SDK stubs in the directory named by GENETICS_STUBS_DIR.

Every view lives in the BigQuery dataset `genetics_results`. Qualify each one as
`genetics_results.<view>`, the way the worked examples below are written: the query service
sets no default dataset, and its fallback that patches an unqualified name is a regular
expression that cannot tell a table position from a string literal.

Each query runs under three ceilings: 25,000 returned rows, 50 GB scanned per query, and 200
GB scanned across one execution. Exceeding any of them raises GeneticsError — a truncated
answer is never returned as a short frame — so aggregate and filter in SQL rather than
fetching every row, and add the partition predicate each view's file names.

| view | summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`credible_sets_v`](credible_sets_v.md) | Fine-mapped credible sets with variant-level posterior inclusion probabilities (PIP). |
| [`colocalization_v`](colocalization_v.md) | Colocalization analysis results (coloc.susie) between pairs of studies. |
| [`coloc_credsets_v`](coloc_credsets_v.md) | Individual credible set variants in colocalized credible sets. |
| [`exome_variant_results_v`](exome_variant_results_v.md) | Single-variant exome association results from multiple resources with different significance thresholds. |
| [`gene_burden_results_v`](gene_burden_results_v.md) | Gene-level burden test results from exome sequencing studies (e.g. |
| [`asm_qtl_v`](asm_qtl_v.md) | Allele-specific methylation QTL (ASM-QTL) results from deCODE Genetics (Stefansson et al. |
| [`open_chromatin_v`](open_chromatin_v.md) | Atlas of accessible/active chromatin regions (peaks) labeled by cell type, tissue, and condition. |
| [`variant_effect_v`](variant_effect_v.md) | In-silico PREDICTED effects of variants on chromatin accessibility from deep-learning models (ChromBPNet and FLARE). |
| [`mpra_v`](mpra_v.md) | MEASURED cis-regulatory allelic activity from a massively parallel reporter assay (Siraj et al. |
| [`hla_associations_v`](hla_associations_v.md) | Classical HLA allele associations from FinnGen R14 — every imputed HLA allele tested against every core R14 endpoint (~2,712 phenotypes x 187 alleles across 10 genes). |
| [`gene_annotations_v`](gene_annotations_v.md) | Whole-universe gene annotations, one row per gene: HGNC core fields joined to GENCODE GRCh38 coordinates, with full-lineage HGNC gene-group arrays (gene_group_ids / gene_group_names contain the leaf group plus all of its ancestor groups, so any group can be matched with `<id> IN UNNEST(gene_group_ids)`). |
| [`variant_annotation_v`](variant_annotation_v.md) | Per-variant functional annotation and FinnGen (R14) allele frequencies — one row per variant, covering all imputed variants, not only fine-mapped ones. |
| [`peak_to_gene_v`](peak_to_gene_v.md) | Open4Gene peak-to-gene links from FinnGen ATAC-seq: which genes a chromatin peak's accessibility is associated with, in which cell type. |
| [`phenotypes_v`](phenotypes_v.md) | Trait/phenotype metadata: the human-readable name, trait type, category and sample sizes behind the opaque phenotype codes the results tables store. |
| [`datasets_v`](datasets_v.md) | Dataset registry: what every `dataset` value appearing in the results views actually is — its resource, version, provenance, description and credible-set caveats. |
